sections.label: Hospitality, from the inside
sections.statement: I help owners turn beautiful properties into places guests remember, <t>and growing groups into one standard of service.</t>
body: For thirty-five years I worked inside IHCL, the company behind the Taj: from a duty manager’s desk at St. James’ Court in London, through fifteen years in Business Excellence, to helping build and scale amã Stays & Trails into a distinctive hospitality brand.
Today I advise, mentor and help hospitality businesses build for the future, bringing the discipline of a great hotel company to the property in front of me.
sections.sign: अतिथि देवो भव · the guest is god

sections.label: Where I am called in
sections.title: Most engagements <t>begin with one of these.</t>
items: A family home that could welcome guests, but has never been run as a business.
A beautiful property whose guests do not come back.
A team that serves well on good days, and only on good days.
A group that is growing faster than its standards.
A new hotel or homestay, still on paper, that needs an operator’s eye before it opens.
A board or founder who wants someone at the table who has run hotels.

sections.title: Four ways <t>I work with you.</t>
sections.lede: Each grows out of a chapter of my career.

items.for: Owners of homestays, villas & boutique hotels
items.d: Concept, the story of the house, pre-opening and standards that still feel like a home.
Common standards, quality systems and the measures that make a portfolio consistent without making it identical.
items.from: Built on fifteen years in Business Excellence

items.from: Built on thirty-five years of leadership at IHCL

items.d: Masterclasses, panels and award juries. Team capability programmes run through HOSPI Sigma.

steps.d: A property is personal. The work starts by hearing the owners out: what the place is, what it means to them and what they want it to become.
The guest experience is built around what makes the place itself, not around a brochure.
Standards and measures the team can keep, so good service is consistent, not occasional.

steps.d: From first-time owner-operators to front-line teams: the confidence to serve well, and to draw a line.

sections.label: The most fulfilling chapter
sections.title: amã Stays <t>& Trails.</t>
sections.body: Families came to us with houses their parents had left them. We listened to the owners, kept what made each house itself, and built a brand around it.

sections.lead: Something I wrote down before a conversation on Inspire Someone Today:
sections.q: “Success is not measured by how many people know your name. It is measured by how many people are better because they crossed your path.”

items.t: Hotels Are Solving the Wrong Problem
